title: Tanzanian Swahili Seafood Platter
community: Zanzibar — the ultimate expression of Indian Ocean seafood
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Swahili Seafood Platter — a spectacular Zanzibar feast of grilled whole fish, coconut prawns, octopus curry, calamari, and tamarind mussels with coconut rice. The Indian Ocean on a single table.
longDesc: The Swahili seafood platter is what the Indian Ocean has to offer — all of it, simultaneously. The skill is in the timing: each seafood has different cooking requirements. At Zanzibar's finest restaurants this platter arrives to silence — followed immediately by conversation about nothing else.
ingredients: 200g large prawns — for coconut sauté (see TZA067)
Coconut rice (TZA002), kachumbari, coconut chutney, pili pili
steps: Prepare coconut rice and octopus curry in advance.
Begin grilling fish 20 minutes before service — basting every 3 minutes.
Cook calamari in a hot pan 2—3 minutes only.
Cook prawns in garlic coconut butter 4 minutes.
Assemble platter: rice at one end, fish centre, prawns, calamari, mussels, octopus in sections.
Scatter coriander. Arrange sauces in small bowls.
chefTips: Stage cooking carefully — octopus and rice done ahead.
Arrange by colour for visual impact.
commonMistakes: Timing errors — overcooked calamari or prawns.
cookingScience: Each seafood has dramatically different optimal cooking times: mussels 4—5 min; calamari 2—3 min; prawns 4 min; fish 20 min. Staging is everything.
sustainabilityTips: All Indian Ocean seafood from local Zanzibar fishermen.
culturalNote: The Zanzibar seafood platter is an expression of gratitude to the Indian Ocean — the sea that has fed, connected, and enriched this island for millennia.
